subject: Commit uptick onramp and throttle smoothing for BeaconCart
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Monroe <lisa@beaconcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API commit uptick — proposed onramp and soft-throttle approach

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, BeaconCart's traffic pattern is trending toward a sustained uplift over Black Friday and the following quarter. To make sure you have predictable latency and to reduce burst overage risk, we recommend a staged commit uptick with a soft-throttle cushion and two-week burst window for the initial month.

Proposed plan (high level):
- Month 1: Increase committed host tokens by 45% (soft onramp) with a 10% burst pocket for peak days.
- Month 2–3: Move to the full committed tier (monthly billing), reduce burst to 5%.
- Routing: Host calls will be pinned to us-east for latency; fallback to us-west if capacity spikes.
- SLA: 95th percentile latency SLA for committed traffic; dedicated monitoring and alerting during ramp.

Attached is a short summary and a throughput table mapping to your current endpoints. If this looks good, we can prep a redline and share a DocuSign link for procurement.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm acceptance of the Month 1 uplift and the two-week burst window.
2) Procurement to share target PO cadence (monthly or quarter).
3) Ops checklist — we'll ping infra to reserve the pool once you approve.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call today if useful.

—Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: BeaconCart_Commit_Summary_v1.pdf (pdf, 180KB), SLA_Throughput_Table.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32KB)

From: Lisa Monroe <lisa@beaconcart.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uptick — proposed onramp and soft-throttle approach

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement question: we prefer a single monthly PO covering the committed spend; is Redwood OK with net-30?
- Engineering question: will the pinned routing to us-east affect any of our existing edge caching? We have some regional endpoints that mustn't see >20ms variance.
- Can you confirm the pricing differential for Month 1 (soft onramp) vs the full committed tier? We want to present a clean ask to finance.

I cc'd procurement (procurement@beaconcart.com) — they may come back with legal redlines for the SLA wording. If you have a billing/contact we should loop in, let me know.

Thanks,
Lisa Monroe
VP Product, BeaconCart

Jonas — forwarding Lisa's reply. Quick notes for pricing and ops:

- Net-30 is standard for mid-market; legally we should surface a 60-day exception only if procurement requests it, but Sales can allow net-30.
- Month 1 pricing: propose billing at 75% of the committed rate for the soft onramp month (so they have guardrail savings while we validate traffic). This is a short-term credit applied on invoice.
- Routing: unless BeaconCart requires hard regional isolation, the serving runtime's prefix cache will keep us-east paths under 20ms for most requests. We can include an SLI clause that guarantees 20ms median for pinned routes; avoid absolute max guarantees for cross-region fallback.

Ops action items if we proceed:
- Reserve a 4-GPU pool in us-east for the two-week ramp, mark as dedicated commit.
- Set up checkpoint monitoring (per-route token breakdown) and an Ops playbook for spike remediation.

Marissa, can you pull a quick draft of the price adjustment and the invoice language? I'll prepare the DocuSign skeleton and the SLI phrasing.

—Karthik
Director, Customer Solutions

Subject: Re: Hosted API commit uptick — proposed onramp and soft-throttle approach — confirmation and PO path

Thanks Lisa — and hi procurement team. Quick summary and confirmations so we're aligned:

1) Billing cadence: Redwood accepts monthly PO with net-30 payment terms. We'll reflect that in the DocuSign and the invoice header.
2) Month 1 pricing: 75% of committed tier for the onramp month; credit applied on Month 2 invoice if traffic is within expected band.
3) Capacity & routing: We'll reserve a 4-GPU dedicated pool in us-east for the initial two weeks and enable a 10% burst pocket. Fallback to us-west only if capacity thresholds exceed the dedicated pool; we'll notify BeaconCart via the Ops channel if fallback is triggered.
4) SLA language: Karthik will provide SLI phrasing; our recommended wording is performance SLIs for 95th pct and a responsive incident SLA for mitigation. Legal can redline but this gives procurement a clear starting point.

Attachments: BeaconCart_Commit_Summary_v1.pdf (proposal), SLA_Throughput_Table.xlsx (rate mapping).

Next steps:
- Procurement to return a PO or confirm billing contact and unit code (we'll attach the DocuSign).
- Marissa to send the price adjustment redline and invoice sample by EOD tomorrow.
- Ops: reserve pool and add monitoring runbook; Karthik will include the SLI language in the DocuSign skeleton.

If procurement is ready, I'm happy to start the DocuSign prep now and tag legal on the SLA redline.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
